text:
jordan: Heads-up — after last night's autotune run we see a regression on A100 narrowband buckets. Median decode latency for 512-token requests went from ~18ms -> ~32ms in prod, and KV eviction rate jumped ~3x. Saved traces here: https://internal/redwood/traces/2123456789 :eyes:

maria: Interesting. Autotune picked fused-kernel for seqlen range 128-1024, but traces show frequent kernel handoffs because batches are tiny at decode time. The overhead of kernel switch + small-batch inefficiency seems to dominate.

akash: Can we rollback the autotune pick quickly? Which flag toggles it?

jordan: The quickest toggle is `runtime.autotune.narrowband.enabled=false`. That's safe but blunt — it disables the whole narrowband branch. We probably want a safer gate: only apply fused-kernel when batch_size >= 8 AND kv_hitrate >= 0.9.

carla: I'm running a short staging test now with hysteresis added: min_samples=50, cooldown=120s. Patch snippet:```json
{
  "autotune": {
    "min_samples": 50,
    "cooldown_s": 120,
    "batch_threshold": 8
  }
}
```

lee: Quick question — why did KV evictions spike? Are we misrouting some short-ctx requests to the prefill path which writes full KV pages?

maria: Looks like it. Prefill_count for seqlen < 64 jumped ~4x in the traces. Prefetch misclassification is causing duplicate KV writes and faster eviction pressure.

akash: Quick mitigation idea: disable prefetch for seqlen < 128 or set `kv.defer_small_prefill=true`. That should lower write amplification while we fix the classifier.

devops-bot: deploy started — rollback/autotune-safety-2123456789 -> staging (job #4367) :rocket:

carla: Staging results from the rollback + hysteresis: median decode down to ~20ms, KV eviction normalized to baseline. Still need longer soak but looks promising.

jordan: Next steps: 1) Add unit/integration tests for narrowband selection so future autotune runs don't regress; 2) instrument histograms for "kernel_pick" per seqlen bucket and expose as per-route metrics; 3) add an alert: `kv_eviction_rate > 1%` sustained over 1m.

lee: I'll open the PR with tests + gating changes — assigning @maria for review.

maria: :thumbsup: I'll review today and verify the traces.

akash: Also think about a cheap-fallback kernel for tiny batches to avoid the heavy kernel swap overhead — I can prototype a tiny-batch kernel that trades some throughput for much lower latency.

jordan: Good idea. If we can short-circuit to a low-latency path for batch<=4 that might remove the worst tail. Let's track as follow-up.

carla: Also adding a short perf regression write-up to the runbook and linking these traces. Will update when PR is up.

lee: Thanks all — feel free to ping if you need help validating perf numbers on non-A100 hardware.

jordan: closing loop — will post final numbers after 24h soak. :white_check_mark:
